No templates found with those criteria. Maybe need to include bonds broken/formed. In Peterson, bond broken: C-Si and C-O (beta-hydroxy silane elimination). But forward reaction: C-Si broken, C-O broken, C=C formed. So broken functional groups: maybe "trimethylsilyl" (lost) and "alcohols"? Actually beta-hydroxy silane has an alcohol (C-O) that is broken. So functional groups broken: "trimethylsilyl", "alcohols"? The list includes "aliphatic hydroxyls", "aromatic hydroxyls". Our substrate has no OH. But template may involve those. Let's search with bonds broken/formed. Need bond types: C-Si is bond between Si (atomic number 14) and C (6). Not sure representation. Might be "6-14". Not sure.

Alternative: maybe we can directly apply a known template ID for Peterson reaction. Could be in dataset. Could search by name? Not possible.

Maybe we can infer precursors manually: The product is stilbene with two anisole rings. The Peterson precursor would be a beta-hydroxy silane: something like (4-methoxyphenyl)C(SiMe3)(OH)CH(4-methoxyphenyl). Actually the carbon skeleton: carbonyl precursor would be a ketone: (4-methoxyphenyl)C(=O)CH(4-methoxyphenyl). That's a diaryl ketone (benzophenone derivative). The silyl reagent is trimethylsilyl carbanion (e.g., Me3SiCH2-). In Peterson, you add silyl carbanion to carbonyl to give beta-hydroxy silane: R2C=O + :CH-SiMe3 -> R2C(OH)-CH(SiMe3). Then elimination yields alkene R2C=CH2? Wait for our case, we need alkene between two aryl groups, not terminal. Actually starting carbonyl is a ketone with two aryl groups: (4-methoxyphenyl)C(=O)(4-methoxyphenyl) i.e., bis(4-methoxyphenyl) ketone (a diaryl ketone). Adding silyl carbanion (Me3SiCH2-) would give beta-hydroxy silane: (Ar)C(OH)(CH2SiMe3)(Ar). Then elimination yields alkene Ar-CH=CH-Ar (stilbene). Yes that matches.

Thus precursors: 1) 4-methoxybenzophenone (i.e., 4-methoxybenzophenone) SMILES: COc1ccc(cc1)C(=O)c2ccc(OC)cc2. That's the ketone. 2) Trimethylsilylmethane (Me3SiCH3) or its carbanion equivalent? The reagent is trimethylsilylmethyl lithium, but as a neutral precursor we can use trimethylsilylmethane (CH3SiMe3) which after deprotonation gives carbanion. So SMILES: C[Si](C)(C)C (that's tetramethylsilane? Actually trimethylsilylmethane is CH3Si(CH3)3: SMILES "C[Si](C)(C)C". Yes.

Thus possible precursor pair: ["COc1ccc(cc1)C(=O)c2ccc(OC)cc2", "C[Si](C)(C)C"].

But there could be alternative: using different silyl reagent like trimethylsilyl chloride + base? But typical Peterson uses silyl carbanion. So likely only one combination.

We need to return list of lists of SMILES strings. So answer: [["COc1ccc(cc1)C(=O)c2ccc(OC)cc2", "C[Si](C)(C)C"]].

Check if any other possibilities: Could also use 4-methoxybenzaldehyde + something? No, need ketone.
